statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-49834 (GO-2026-5952, GHSA-9vcr-p3rj-q5q6): in sigstore-go, a verifier configured to require more than one transparency log entry or signed certificate timestamp counts entries per entry rather than per log, so one compromised log can satisfy a multi-log threshold. It is fixed in sigstore-go 1.2.0. The Go vulnerability database lists no symbols; the fix commit changes VerifyTlogEntry in pkg/verify/tlog.go and VerifySignedCertificateTimestamp in pkg/verify/sct.go. Sources: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5952, https://github.com/sigstore/sigstore-go/security/advisories/GHSA-9vcr-p3rj-q5q6, https://github.com/sigstore/sigstore-go/commit/dbb07e62623edd5b175fb9dd5a41dcb85a159207 . We checked every published trivy-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 38 builds, 0.69.1-r0 to the current 0.74.0-r12, each for x86_64 and aarch64, each verified against the repository index checksum. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/trivy, a statically linked Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0. We read its Go build information (go version -m) and its function table (go tool nm), and searched its raw bytes, which also finds the names of inlined functions. The Go build information lists github.com/sigstore/sigstore-go 1.1.4 in builds up to 0.71.2-r2, inside the affected range, and 1.2.1 in 0.71.2-r3; builds from 0.73.0-r0 on do not contain the module. In every build that contains it, the only sigstore-go functions in the function table are the package initializers github.com/sigstore/sigstore-go/pkg/bundle.init and github.com/sigstore/sigstore-go/pkg/verify.init; neither VerifyTlogEntry nor VerifySignedCertificateTimestamp, nor any other pkg/verify function, is present, while runtime.main is. The raw-byte search of every build finds no VerifyTlogEntry or VerifySignedCertificateTimestamp string; the pkg/verify names it finds are the initializer, the treeIDSuffixRegex variable it sets up, and the source path of tlog.go where that variable is declared. As a positive control, the same function-table and byte searches on a program built against sigstore-go 1.1.4 that calls both functions find verify.VerifyTlogEntry and verify.VerifySignedCertificateTimestamp. The control programs were built with Go 1.27.1, CGO_ENABLED=0, for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. The vulnerable code is not in the shipped binary.
